questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code records HTTP request metrics? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client disconnects while a request is being handled and the server drops the handler future. What happens to the in-flight gauge?
choices: It stays incremented forever, because the code after `next.run(req).await` never runs
It is decremented by InFlightGuard's Drop implementation when the future is dropped
It is reset by `metrics::render()` on the next scrape
It is decremented by the status counter code in `track`

questions.prompt: A request takes 300 ms. Which histogram buckets (le) of tracking_http_request_duration_seconds are incremented for it?
choices: Every bucket with le of 0.5 and above, including +Inf

questions.prompt: Why does main() call `metrics::init()` before building the router?
choices: It makes registration happen at startup, so a failure such as a duplicate metric name panics immediately instead of on the first request that touches the metric
Without it the metrics would never be registered, because Lazy statics are registered at program start
It resets all counters to zero so that they restart on each deploy
It starts a background thread that gathers the metrics
